p: Folly Farm sits in a sweet spot for holidaymakers. South Pembrokeshire's best-known resorts are all a short drive away, and the Pembrokeshire Coast National Park, the only coastal national park in Britain, is right on the doorstep.

Tenby is the obvious base, with its pastel harbour, medieval town walls and four beaches. From the harbour, boats sail across to Caldey Island in the warmer months, where Cistercian monks still live and work, making chocolate and perfume from the island's flowers. It's a peaceful, fascinating outing and the boat trip is half the fun.

Saundersfoot, just along the coast, is a smaller, friendly resort with a sandy beach and a busy little harbour, perfect for crabbing off the harbour wall. Amroth has a long beach that reveals a submerged forest at very low tides.

For more animal time, Manor Wildlife Park at St Florence, near Tenby, is a smaller safari-style park that pairs well with Folly Farm for a second day. If the kids want bigger thrills, Oakwood, a theme park near Narberth, is only a short drive north.

At Folly Farm, it's worth getting there close to opening time in summer holidays, as it's very popular with families staying locally. Start with the zoo while it's cooler, then head for the farm and the indoor rides later on. Wipes and a spare change of clothes are a good idea with little ones in the farmyard. Put it all together and south Pembrokeshire can easily fill a week of family holiday.
